kf: **Bullous pemphigoid (BP)** is the commonest autoimmune blistering disease: tense blisters in older people.
Often starts with weeks to months of **itch** and urticarial plaques before blisters (prodrome).
Autoantibodies against **BP180 and BP230** at the basement membrane; confirm with biopsy and immunofluorescence.
Localised: clobetasol; mild–moderate: **doxycycline 200 mg once daily** (BLISTER trial: safer than prednisolone).
Check drugs: **DPP-4 inhibitors (gliptins)**, diuretics, checkpoint inhibitors; associated with neurological disease (stroke, dementia, Parkinson's).

sub: Mostly over 70; incidence rising with age and drugs; UK about 4,000 new cases a year.

aet: Autoimmunity to hemidesmosome proteins; drug triggers (gliptins, loop diuretics, spironolactone, PD-1 inhibitors).
myths: **"Blisters in older people are just friction"**: itchy urticarial plaques with tense blisters need biopsy.
patho_lead: Antibodies attack the **anchors holding the epidermis to the dermis**, so it separates as a tense blister.

mech.t: IgG autoantibodies bind BP180 (collagen XVII) and BP230 in hemidesmosomes.
Complement activation recruits eosinophils and neutrophils that release proteases.
The whole epidermis lifts off: a **tense, roofed blister** (unlike flaccid pemphigus).
mech.cap: BP splits below the epidermis (tense blister); pemphigus splits within it (flaccid).

mech.t: Flexures, limbs and trunk; mucosa involved in a minority.

histo: Subepidermal blister with eosinophils; direct IF: linear IgG and C3 along the basement membrane; serum BP180/BP230 ELISA.

sub: Whole-body clobetasol is effective but impractical without carers; doxycycline is often preferred.

comp: Infection, sepsis, side effects of steroids; mortality about 20–40% in the first year in frail patients.
prog: Usually remits over 1–5 years with treatment; relapses common.
